input_authorities.input: BYO registration is the source-build/development path; shared project registration remains gated by ADR-012, publisher governance, signed distribution, and release controls
exclusive copy-validate-encrypt-verify-swap migration state machine; older binary refuses to write a newer schema or ciphertext version; R-21/R-22 critical risk rows
any bridge certificate or trust is completely removed on disconnect and uninstall; failure of any trust-cleanup step blocks the add-in rather than leaving orphaned trust
diagnostics allowlist is empty; any future diagnostic export needs an exact content-free schema plus ADR-012, G-PRIV, G-RELEASE, and G-SEC-AUDIT

byo_public_client.configuration: placeholder-only tracked configuration; no real client ID, tenant ID, or other Microsoft identifier in the repository, and no secret on a command line or in tracked configuration
byo_public_client.authentication_limitation: PKCE does not authenticate the binary requesting a token; it authenticates only the authorization-code exchange

shared_project_registration.status: disabled; a separately gated future option
required_governance_controls: dedicated organizational publisher tenant and a verified domain
accurate name, logo, homepage, privacy statement, terms, and support contact
at least two controlled registration owners and an owner-recovery procedure
exact registered redirects with no unused platform configuration
incremental consent and plain-language permission explanations
support for tenants that disable user consent or require admin approval
sign-in/consent-failure monitoring without message or task content collection
signed official builds and updates with published provenance
BYO registration documentation for organizations that reject the shared application

update_trust_chain.metadata_signing: signed independently of package signing; compromising one signing key does not silently authorize the other artifact class
update_trust_chain.key_inventory: a trusted-key inventory records every signing key's purpose, holder, and rotation/revocation procedure; a revoked or rotated key can no longer produce accepted metadata or a package
update_trust_chain.version_policy: monotonic anti-downgrade; an older binary refuses to write a newer schema or ciphertext version, and the client refuses update metadata whose version is not strictly greater than the currently installed version regardless of signature validity
update_trust_chain.channel_binding: update metadata is bound to an exact release channel; a client on one channel never accepts metadata signed for another channel
update_trust_chain.expiry: metadata carries an explicit expiry; expired metadata is refused even if otherwise validly signed
update_trust_chain.package_identity: metadata pins the exact package hash and exact package size; a package matching neither, or only one, is refused before any part of it is applied
update_trust_chain.staging_and_replacement: atomic and protected; a downloaded package is verified completely before staging, staging occurs where the current build cannot yet execute or the current data cannot yet reach, and replacement of the running installation is a single atomic step with a recovery path if it does not complete
update_trust_chain.provenance: must be verifiable to the exact public source revision that produced the package; a package that cannot be tied to an inspectable source revision is refused regardless of valid signatures
update_trust_chain.elevation: no installation or update step elevates privileges by default; any future elevation requires a separate explicit justification and its own review

artifact_boundary.allowlist_rule: every artifact class released or packaged has an explicit allowlist; an artifact outside its class's allowlist is rejected before release rather than filtered afterward
artifact_boundary.sbom_and_provenance: required for every release; a release without either is incomplete
artifact_boundary.npm_publishability: disabled in Phase 0; package.json stays "private": true with an empty files allowlist
artifact_boundary.cargo_publishability: disabled in Phase 0; every workspace crate stays publish = false
artifact_boundary.canary_and_public_repo_gates: run at every required release point (staged commit, push, and package dry run) and never print a suspected secret or identifier value when they fail; a failing gate blocks the release rather than being silenced or bypassed

installer_boundary.install_mode: per-user and unelevated, matching ADR-001's runtime boundary; no administrator rights requested by default
installer_boundary.uninstall_completeness: repeats disconnect cleanup where possible and removes every local bridge trust, certificate, and protocol registration ADR-010 created, leaving no orphaned trust behind
installer_boundary.residual_risk_disclosure: OS paging, backups, snapshots, and endpoint-security exposure are disclosed limitations, not a physical-erasure claim, matching ADR-005 and ADR-PRIV-001
installer_boundary.microsoft_artifact_handling: zero Graph mutation and no bulk deletion of a Microsoft artifact by the uninstaller; existing artifacts are handled per the user's own disconnect choice

diagnostics_rule.future_export_requirement: an exact content-free schema plus ADR-012, G-PRIV, G-RELEASE, and G-SEC-AUDIT; none of those four is satisfied by this ADR and none may be represented as satisfied by a partial subset
